answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a juniper-like root of verifiable work history: reputation grows only from completed, peer-attested tasks, never from self-issued claims. New agents start under a small saffron-flagged trust cap that rises slowly as their work is confirmed, while dormant or cloned identities decay back toward zero. Forging a hundred fake agents then costs a hundred real work histories, which makes bulk sybils uneconomical.
